summary: The frozen N8 Chinese and English texts pass independent scientific, fidelity and readability review within their explicitly simplified molecular model. No repair is required. This is text approval only; fig-05, native stages and product acceptance are not approved.

independence.basis: Independent claim-by-claim reading of native source text and both modern locales, not adoption of the author's findings or mechanical passes.
independence.authorReportTreatment: Read after the source and templates as a record of intended qualifications and inherited checks, not as an independent verdict.
independence.authorizationTreatment: The human's explicit reversible narrative-qualification authorization permits sound modern scientific clarification. Each clarification was judged for its actual science and bilingual meaning rather than rejected merely for not being verbatim.

authorCollected.usage: Byte-hash binding only, not an independent content verdict.

independentClaimCoverage.scope: Each of the authorized 13 source blocks per locale, including the footnote, empty figure placeholder and caption; no source-row counting or new source-scan review.
independentClaimCoverage.referenceConvention: inputKey resolves to the absolute, hash-bound path in inputBinding. JSON pointers are zero-based. Source pointers refer to nativeLesson.

claimsReviewed: Resistance to breaking a thick stick illustrates strong microscopic cohesion.
The stick consists of molecules.
Adult handling and splinter/fragment precautions.
blocks.independentAssessment: The qualitative illustration is retained without claiming a numerical pair-force measurement. Both languages turn the source invitation into adult-handled, safe prose rather than an exercise. Chinese's additional no-bare-hand warning reinforces, rather than contradicts, the English adult-only caution.

claimsReviewed: Attraction supports condensed matter in the simplified molecular-cohesion model.
Attraction alone does not give a stable arrangement.
Strong close-range repulsion resists unlimited interpenetration.
blocks.independentAssessment: The simplified-model scope appropriately removes the original universal claim about every substance under every condition while retaining its cohesion argument. Resistance to indefinite compression is compatible with finite electron-cloud overlap in the later block; neither language describes molecules as strictly non-overlapping rigid objects.

claimsReviewed: Atoms contain electrons and nuclei; molecules are composed of atoms.
Neutral molecules can have strong short-distance electrical interactions.
Neighboring charged constituents interact.
Internal motion and intermolecular forces require a quantum account.
Only a qualitative distance-dependent pair interaction is introduced here.
blocks.independentAssessment: Electrical neutrality is not confused with absence of electric interaction. The quantum qualification prevents the two-component model being presented as a complete fixed-charge explanation, including of overlap repulsion. It does not introduce an unsupported classical electron trajectory, new formula or task. The Chinese and English retain the same microscopic constituents, complexity and restricted explanatory aim.

claimsReviewed: Oppositely charged constituents.
Attractive and repulsive model contributions act in opposite directions.
The signed net component is repulsive magnitude minus attractive magnitude.
blocks.independentAssessment: The texts distinguish positive magnitudes from signed projections. Their specified outward-positive convention makes the subtraction unambiguous and agrees with the later graph prose. The charge statement is retained without claiming that fixed-charge Coulomb forces alone explain every contribution.

claimsReviewed: Repulsion grows more rapidly than attraction on close approach in the model.
Electron-shell overlap is associated with an especially steep rise in repulsion.
Footnote marker connects this discussion to the projection qualification.
blocks.independentAssessment: The close-distance restriction avoids a global claim about component growth throughout all separations. In context, growth concerns contribution strengths, while the footnote and adjacent blocks define their directional signs. Electron-shell overlap is explicitly preserved in both languages; no exact shell radius or universal repulsive exponent is asserted.

claimsReviewed: The relevant force quantities are components along the line joining the atomic centers.
Component signs encode direction.
blocks.independentAssessment: The source qualification is not dropped or converted to unsigned total-vector magnitudes. English 'components' faithfully renders Chinese 'projections'; both state the line and directional meaning of the signs.

claimsReviewed: Source-described upper repulsive, lower attractive and middle net curves.
Repulsion positive and attraction negative along the line of centers.
Approximate radii-sum equilibrium distance r_0.
Equal contribution magnitudes and zero net force at equilibrium.
At r>r_0 attraction dominates, F<0 and molecules are pulled together.
As r tends to infinity, F tends to zero.
At r<r_0 repulsion dominates, F>0 and molecules are pushed apart.
blocks.independentAssessment: All force signs and motions agree with the declared convention. Equal nonzero opposing contributions, not absence of both contributions, give zero net force at r_0. The radii-sum wording is approximate and model-bound. Both sides of equilibrium and the infinity limit retain their source narrative order. These qualitative relationships can be judged from the source text without viewing fig-05; no claim about actual curve pixels or a completed figure is made.

claimsReviewed: The empty text placeholder keeps source figure identity fig-05.
English label is Figure 5.
blocks.independentAssessment: Text-only inspection finds no new scientific statement, task, answer or claim of a completed image. The placeholder is faithful, and its label is correctly localized. Science pass here applies only to the absence of conflicting text; the figure itself remains not reviewed.

claimsReviewed: Caption identifies Figure 5, without adding interpretive data.
blocks.independentAssessment: Chinese retains the source caption and English translates it accurately. No extra curve label, numerical value or scientific assertion is introduced. This caption verdict is not image approval.

claimsReviewed: Distance-dependent net interaction explains compression and tension restoring forces.
Below r_0 the net force opposes closer approach.
Slight stretching from near equilibrium makes attraction dominate.
Return toward initial positions is restricted to small recoverable elastic deformation.
Arbitrary separation or fracture is not guaranteed to reverse.
blocks.independentAssessment: Compression and extension restore in the directions already established. 'Tends toward' preserves restoring action without promising automatic settling, global reunion or repair after fracture. The near-equilibrium and elastic restrictions are present in both languages and are scientifically appropriate clarifications of the source.

claimsReviewed: Interaction usually becomes practically negligible beyond several molecular sizes in the neutral-molecule model.
Short-range means rapid weakening, not an abrupt finite-distance cutoff.
A nonzero distant attractive tail is compatible with the preceding signs and infinity limit.
blocks.independentAssessment: The source's several-times size scale remains qualitative, not an exact threshold. Both languages distinguish negligibility from literal zero. Read with F<0 for finite r>r_0 and the infinity limit, this preserves a weak nonzero tail and does not replace it with a force that stops at a specified finite distance.

claimsReviewed: Small displacement produces a net force directed toward equilibrium on either side.
Net restoring-force magnitude is approximately linear in displacement.
The source-described short thick net-force segment is locally approximated as straight.
Hooke's law relates elastic-force magnitude to small elastic deformation.
Large molecular displacement invalidates this local linear approximation.
blocks.independentAssessment: The modern texts correctly attach linearity to the net restoring force, not separately to attractive and repulsive contributions that balance at equilibrium. The zero-net equilibrium, both restoring directions, approximate straight segment and small-elastic range are mutually consistent. A bent global curve is not described as globally Hookean. No image observation is claimed.

claimsReviewed: Macroscopic total deformation is distributed across many neighboring molecular layers.
Each local distance change must remain small.
Total deformation may exceed a million molecular sizes while Hooke's law remains applicable.
The deformation must remain elastic; large absolute length change is not large local displacement or unrestricted strain.
blocks.independentAssessment: The million-times comparison retains its numerical scale and refers to total length deformation, not a million-fold stretch of each molecular spacing. Both languages explicitly require small local changes and elastic behavior. Replacing 'all distances' with many participating neighboring layers avoids an unjustified universal deformation pattern while preserving the source's microscopic-to-macroscopic argument.

zh.basis: Complete independent reading of the title, all authorized blocks, footnote, caption, figure-manifest labels and the empty exercise template.
zh.readability: Concrete actions introduce cohesion; subsequent sentences identify constituents, define the sign convention, interpret equilibrium and then explain elasticity. Terms for overlap, signed projection, net force, small displacement and total deformation stay consistent. The quantities and their conditions are understandable without importing an unstated global force law.
zh.fidelity: All source concepts survive the authorized scientific qualifications. No task is invented from the stick-breaking illustration.

en.basis: Complete independent reading against the native Chinese source and modern Chinese counterpart, including each condition, sign, quantity and reference.
en.readability: The title is accurate. Sentence subjects and force directions are explicit. 'Components', 'net force', 'overlap', 'recoverable elastic deformation', 'negligible' and 'a million times' carry the same scientific meanings as their Chinese counterparts. Paragraph grouping differs without changing logical order or dropping a condition.
en.fidelity: No scientific or quantitative mistranslation found. The English adult-handling precaution covers the safety intent; the Chinese adds an explicit bare-hand warning without a semantic conflict.
en.metadataBoundary: Chinese chapter, section and printed_title fields remain source identities. The author's claimed TOC-based rendered localization was not independently rendered or approved here; it is not evidence of a body-text translation omission.

languageAssessment.bilingualConditions: Both locales retain simplified-model scope, quantum completeness, close-approach scope, approximate equilibrium distance, near-equilibrium recoverability, neutral-molecule short-range scope, local linearity and elastic small-layer changes.
languageAssessment.readabilityBoundary: Textual readability only. No render, layout, font, pixel or learner usability acceptance is claimed.

taskAndManifestAssessment.assessment: The native source has zero original questions, and both frozen modern exercise templates remain empty. The source's stick-breaking invitation remains prose, not an invented question, choice or answer.

figureManifestText.assessment: Labels and fig-05 identity agree with the lesson text. Source PNG/SVG and spec references were read only as manifest text; none of those files was opened, rendered, checked or approved.

sourceMathOrder.assessment: Independent narrative reading preserves the source sequence: Figure 5, approximate r_0 and zero net force; r>r_0 with negative F; the infinity-to-zero limit; r<r_0 with positive F; compression below r_0; then Figure 5's local straight segment. Signs and their physical interpretations agree in both locales. This is not a fresh token-order, delimiter or KaTeX checker result.
